subject.title: [Feature]: Self-evolving SOUL.md via opt-in reflection sub-turn + soul_update tool

question: Should OpenClaw core allow opt-in model-mediated writes to SOUL.md, and what security contract must that persistence path satisfy before merge?
rationale: This changes a durable instruction surface loaded into future sessions, so automation cannot choose the core-vs-plugin owner boundary or the acceptable prompt-injection risk contract.

options.title: Review linked PR as the decision surface
options.body: Continue with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95793 only if maintainers accept the default-off SOUL persistence direction and require the security/upgrade proof there.

options.title: Move the idea out of core
options.body: Reject core auto-updates for now and ask for a memory-plugin or plugin-API design if maintainers want durable preference capture without mutating SOUL.md directly.

options.title: Close the direction
options.body: Close this issue and the linked candidate if maintainers decide SOUL.md should remain manually edited only.

recommendation.title: Review linked PR as the decision surface
recommendation.body: Continue with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95793 only if maintainers accept the default-off SOUL persistence direction and require the security/upgrade proof there.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has direct SOUL documentation and agent runtime/config history and is the strongest available owner for the product/security boundary choice.
